rulings.rationale: DECIDING FACT: four filed 12-month years (2018, 2019, 2020, 2024) and not one positive Part-I count in any lane in any year — a channel that has never once demonstrated it can carry an offence. Provenance side: blank-as-zero is excluded (the 2024 CIUS printed zero sits on a 12-month NIBRS header, not a 0-2-month submission), and the CIUS/SRS/NIB agreement is one submission rendered three times, not corroboration, so the only real evidence is a single submission of twelve zero months. Composition side: all seven streams zero, so composition can neither support nor undercut — it is not a thin year with an odd shape, it is a uniform zero, which is what an RMS zero-report emitter produces. Absolute plausibility: at FBIpop 977 the peer band implies ~4.9 Part-I/yr, ~20 over the four filed years; even at half peer rate P(zero across all four) is ~5e-5. Larceny alone would have to be absent for four filed years in a town of ~980. Aggravating: the ORI went fully dark 2021-2023 (SRS 0 months, no NIB row at all), so its filing is intermittent, and the gap years are consistent with policing having passed to the Gray County sheriff while the ORI kept a nominal filing status. No succession question — the ORI is live on the 2024 roster with an exclusive w=1 footprint on Montezuma city (place 2047875).

rulings.detail: Carry the published 0 as observed for 2024; no repair, no uplift, no fill. The SRS 1-month row is not a coverage claim about the year — for a NIBRS reporter the SRS lane is a back-conversion rendering, and the NIBRS batch header (12 months) is the submission record. rulings.detail: 2024 should go MISSING and fillable for OH0070300. If a supervisor re-opens any single case here, make it this one. Fill: anchor on the recent credible full years (2022 CIUS 5, 2023 NIB 4 on 11mo -> level ~4-6) rather than the 16/yr baseline, since part of the decline is probably real. No succession issue: on the 2024 roster, single exclusive w=1 footprint (place 3908560, Bridgeport village).
rulings.rationale: Two facts push it over the line despite the clean reporting history. First, ABSOLUTE PLAUSIBILITY: FBIpop 1,522 is above the 1,500 floor and capacity-then-zero fired (full 12-month positive years through 2022), so per doctrine a capacity-then-zero at this population reads as structural non-reporting; peer median 702.6/100k implies ~11 offences and the agency's own baseline mix is 16/yr with larceny 10.3, which cannot go to absolute zero as a level change. Second, PROVENANCE breaks in 2024 in a way it never had before: Return-A submitted months run 11, 11, 12, 7, 7, 6 for 2018-2023 and then collapse to 1 in 2024, so the only support for a complete year is the NIBRS header while the other rendering of the same submission says the record stopped. COMPOSITION cannot arbitrate (2024 is uniformly zero, and the packet notes the 16/yr base is too small to score), which is why this is medium and not high -- the hypothesis that a shrinking Rust Belt village genuinely stepped from 4 to 0 is not excluded, only outweighed.

The level evidence points the other way: the ORI's single informative year (2023: 1 offence, corroborated at 12 NIBRS months) makes a zero the modal draw, so a thin genuine zero is entirely consistent with its history, and the 2020-2022 SRS 0-month rows are non-reports that carry no information either way. Medium rather than high only because FBIpop 2,060 is above the 1,500 line - but the footprint is a rural New England township, not a compact city, and three consecutive full-year NIBRS records at 1-3 are a better estimate of this agency's level than a population-band median built mostly on denser places.

rulings.rationale: The 2024 NIBRS batch header carries 12 submitted months, which rules out BLANK-AS-ZERO (that artefact needs a 0-2 month record), and the prior review's decisive claim - that 0-month SRS is a structural-zero warning - does not survive checking. Across this ORI's whole series the SRS month count tracks months with transmitted CONTENT, not submission: 2021 (1 offence) shows SRS 3mo against NIB 11mo, 2022 (0 offences) SRS 1mo against NIB 12mo, 2023-24 (0 offences) SRS 0mo against NIB 12mo. For a NIBRS reporter the FBI back-converts to Return-A, so a zero total yields no Return-A month; SRS 0mo is a derived consequence of the zero, not a second lane disagreeing with it. What remains is a live channel that demonstrably transmits positive content (the 2021 aggravated assault came through the same NIBRS feed), FBIpop 982 credited to an active PD in every year (so this is not an ORI filing over territory Sibley County SO polices - the FBI would zero the population-served field), and an own transmitted level of ~0.26 offences/yr over 46 covered months. At pop 982 with that own level, a zero year is an ordinary outcome; the shape is not never-positive and not capacity-then-zero, and pop sits inside the sub-1,000 carve-out where zero is absolutely plausible.

rulings.detail: Carry the published 0 for 2024 as observed, no uplift and no fill; 2022 and 2023 the same. The 2019-2021 rows are partial-coverage zeros (3, 10, 8 NIBRS months) and carry very little information either way - do not treat them as corroborating full years.
rulings.rationale: Same provenance test as Henderson and it passes the same way: a 12-month 2024 NIBRS batch header rules out blank-as-zero, and the SRS 0-month figure the prior review leaned on is a back-conversion artefact - this ORI shows SRS 7mo in 2018 when it had 1 offence and SRS 0mo in every year with a zero total, i.e. SRS months follow content. Six consecutive zero years is not, however, six full-coverage zeros: only 2022-2024 reach 12 months. Against that, the agency's own transmitted level is ~0.2 offences/yr (1 larceny in roughly 60 covered months, 2018, transmitted through the same NIBRS lane so the channel is not a dead pipe), FBIpop 740-753 is credited to an active PD in every year rather than to Wadena County SO, and pop 740 is inside the sub-1,000 range where an all-zero Part-I year is a reachable crime outcome. There is no capacity to lose - the agency has never had a year above 1 - so the capacity-then-zero pattern does not apply, and composition is uniformly zero, so it can neither support nor undercut. The honest reading is a real near-zero jurisdiction with a thin but functioning feed, not a non-report.

rulings.detail: 2024 must not stand as an observed 12-month zero; the agency-year goes MISSING and fillable, and 2018-2023 should be treated identically. Own-history fill is unavailable (no real report exists in any year of the panel), so the repair basis is the sheriff peer band (1000,2500] median of 470.3 per 100k applied to FBIpop 1,409, i.e. roughly 6-7 Part-I offences for 2024. The mass lands on the Montana non-municipal remainder, so the repair is a remainder-level correction, not a place-level one.
rulings.rationale: Seven consecutive complete (12-month) NIBRS years with never a single Part-I incident, for the only law-enforcement agency covering an entire county of ~1,400 people. This is precisely the named structural-non-reporting pattern: a never-positive multi-year history at pop >1,000. The peer-implied level is lambda 6.6/yr, which makes even ONE zero year a ~1-in-760 event and the seven-year run arithmetically unreachable; sustaining it would require a true county rate of ~35 per 100k, about a fourteenth of the band median, which is not a reachable crime outcome for 1,400 residents with exclusive county-wide coverage including all unincorporated territory. Every check that could rescue it is absent rather than favourable: no publication lane carries this ORI in any year (the CIUS ingest covers city/university/state-tribal tables, not county, so the absence is ingest coverage and carries no FBI quality signal either way), SRS is 0-months in all seven years so there is no independent lane, and composition is uniformly zero across all seven streams so it carries no signal. The 12-month header only establishes that twelve batches were filed, not that any records sat behind them - and an administratively perfect feed that has never once transmitted an incident is a non-report the pipeline read as data. Contrast Terrell County in this same batch: half the population and a third of the peer-implied rate, plus agency-supplied SRS-era zero returns and a proven non-filing year that shows its panel distinguishes filing from not filing. Carter has neither.

rulings.detail: Carry the published 2 (1 aggravated assault + 1 larceny) as observed. No uplift - the 12 months are genuinely submitted - and no fill. The lane check the packet asked for comes back clean: no larger equally complete submission was discarded.
rulings.rationale: The agency's own series already contains a comparable trough, which is the fact that decides it: 2021 recorded 1 offence on 10 reported months, sitting between 11 (2020) and 8 (2022). A total of 2 on 12 months in 2024 is inside this ORI's own observed range, not a break from it, so the drop from the 7-8 level is slope, and slope alone does not condemn a positive record. Provenance points the same way: month coverage IMPROVED in the year the count fell (11 months in 2020/2021/2022/2023, 12 in 2024 - the first complete year in the series), which is the opposite of a reporting collapse. The apparent SRS/NIBRS conflict the prior review stopped on is a lane-rendering artefact, not missing data: this ORI's SRS months run chronically below its NIBRS months in every year while the totals match exactly (2020 NIB 11mo/SRS 7mo both totalling 11; 2022 11mo/7mo both 8; 2023 11mo/8mo both 7), so SRS 7mo in 2024 does not indicate five missing months. All three 2024 lanes agree at 2, so the ladder discarded nothing. Absolute plausibility passes - 2 offences at pop 1,513 is 132 per 100k, well inside what villages of that size report - and composition is mixed across one violent and one property stream with no stream visibly dark, so the composition test neither fires nor rescues.

rulings.detail: Do not carry 15 as a measured 12-month total. The record is internally inconsistent about its own coverage, and that is what the flag must say: the violent stream is consistent with a full year (8 aggravated assaults = 118 per 100k, ~98% of the peer-implied expectation of 8.2), while the property streams are consistent with barely one month (4 burglary + 3 larceny = 7 against the ~64 property offences the peer median implies for 6,761 residents, i.e. 11%). No single month ratio repairs both - the year is ~12 believable months for aggravated assault and ~1-2 for property - so an uplift is not available and must not be invented. Flag the agency-year as token/partial, mark the property streams unmeasured and fillable, and do not publish 15 as observed at weight 1.0. Separately, and independently of this ruling: the footprint is the Pennsylvania statewide overlap layer via fallback_overlap, which smears this department's mass across the whole state instead of its Armstrong County service area; that needs its own repair.
rulings.rationale: Composition, not slope, decides it. Larceny at 3 offences for 6,761 residents is 44 per 100k - roughly a tenth of the lowest credible municipal larceny floor and ~7% of the peer-implied larceny level - while aggravated assault sits at essentially its full expected level. Aggravated assault therefore accounts for 53% of this agency's 2024 Part-I total against a normal small-borough share of roughly 5-12%: an inverted composition, which is the signature of an untransmitted property stream rather than of a genuinely quiet jurisdiction. That reading is corroborated by provenance rather than resting on the peer gap alone: FBIpop is 0 through 2022 and 6,854 from 2023, so this is a newly stood-up regional department whose only prior filing is 2 offences on 8 months in 2023, and 2024 is its first full Return-A year; it is not a NIBRS reporter, SRS is the only lane present, and no CIUS or state publication exists to arbitrate. A brand-new department transmitting its violent stream in full and almost none of its property stream is a token record published as complete.

rulings.detail: 2024 must not stand as a tier-high, weight-1.0 observed zero. Mark the agency-year MISSING and fillable, and repair from the agency's OWN recent level, not from peers: 2023 (1 offence on 7 months, ~1.7/yr) and 2022 (6) bracket it, so roughly 1-3 Part-I offences. Explicitly do NOT publish the (0,1000] peer median (503.4 per 100k on FBIpop 766 = ~3.9) into a 766-person place on this evidence. The record that would settle it and is not in the packet: whether the 2024 12-month NIBRS feed carries any Group B / Part-II content (arrests, drug, DUI, simple assault, criminal mischief). Real non-index activity behind those twelve headers flips this to genuine_zero_year and the observed 0 should be restored; a completely empty 12-month feed confirms the ruling.
rulings.rationale: What separates Savoy from the other sub-1,000 zeros in this batch is that its own record establishes a materially positive rate which the hard zero contradicts. Henderson and Sebeka transmit ~0.2-0.26 offences/yr; Savoy transmitted 16 Part-I offences over 42 covered months (~4.6/yr, ABOVE its own band's peer-implied 3.9), including 5 in 2021 and 6 in 2022, before publishing an all-seven-stream zero. P(0) is ~1% against that pooled level and ~3% against a decay-weighted one; only against 2023 alone (1 offence on 7 months) does it become ordinary at ~18%, and a single seven-month draw is the weakest of the available rate estimates. Neither known-artefact test discriminates here - the 12-month header rules out blank-as-zero, the SRS 0-month figure is the back-conversion artefact this ORI shows in every zero-content year, and a uniform zero carries no composition signal - so the ruling rests on absolute plausibility against the agency's own demonstrated level, and there it fails. The asymmetry settles the direction: publishing this as observed x7 at tier high asserts, at the panel's highest confidence, that a 766-person town had no Part-I crime, on a 1-3% event and on a lane (CIUS) that is the same submission re-rendered; the alternative repair is ~2 offences drawn from the agency's own 2022-23 record, which is cheap and defensible. Confidence low because the header jump from 7 to 12 months in exactly the year content went to zero reads equally as compliance improvement (Texas's 2024 NIBRS push) and as a header-only automated feed, and nothing in the packet chooses.

rulings.detail: Carry the published 0 for 2024 as observed, no uplift and no fill; 2018, 2019, 2021, 2022 and 2023 the same, and 2020 correctly stays a 0-month non-report rather than a zero. The mass is the Texas non-municipal remainder for 674 people, so the stake either way is negligible. Record the weak point on the row: the six-year never-positive run only holds if the true rate is well below the band median, and a second independent lane (Texas DPS/CJIS county UCR table for Terrell County) would still be worth pulling if this class is ever revisited in bulk.
rulings.rationale: This is the one micro-county sheriff in the batch where absolute plausibility genuinely passes. 674 residents in a county with no incorporated municipality (Sanderson is a CDP) at ~0.3 people per square mile, against a (0,1000] sheriff peer median of 356.3 per 100k, implies lambda ~2.4/yr - so a single zero year is a ~9% outcome, not an impossibility. That is a third of Carter County's implied rate at half the population, which is the principled line between the two cases. Second, and this is the fact the prior review did not use: the filings are affirmative rather than defaults. 2018 and 2019 are SRS 12-month zero returns at tier high from the era when months_reported was agency-supplied - the strongest form in which an agency can assert a real zero year - and 2020 is a 0-month non-report, which proves this ORI's panel distinguishes 'filed a zero year' from 'filed nothing'. The 12-month rows are therefore real submissions, not an automatic floor. Third, FBIpop is credited to the SO in every year, so this is not an ORI filing over territory another agency polices. The SRS 0-month rows in 2021-2024 are the standard NIBRS back-conversion artefact (a zero total produces no Return-A month) and are not an independent lane dissenting.

rulings.detail: 2024 must not be carried as an observed 0 at tier high, 7-of-7. The agency-year goes MISSING and fillable. No own history exists to fill from - 2018-2023 are 0-month absences, not observed zeros - so the repair basis is the neighbour/peer set: same-county, size-matched DeKalb County village agencies published Part-I of 7 (Kingston), 7 (Somonauk), 19 (Hinckley), 23 (Cortland) and 3 on 9 months (Kirkland), and the (1000,2500] local_police peer median of 702.6 per 100k on FBIpop 1,417 implies ~10. A fill in the 7-10 range is defensible; 0 is not. When 2025 lands it retroactively settles the case - a normal 15-35 incident stream confirms the onboarding artefact, a second near-empty year would justify restoring the zero.
rulings.rationale: The 12-month batch header is a self-declaration with almost nothing behind it, and the content is what decides this rather than the level. The entire 2024 incident stream for this ORI is two incidents (2024-04-30 counterfeiting/forgery, 2024-08-03 animal cruelty), neither Part-I, with Group A/B submitted flags firing in only 3 of 12 months. Two incidents a year is not a credible case volume for a village police department with its own sworn officers and three patrol vehicles - so the defect is a hollow feed, not a genuinely index-free year, and 'the sheriff handles everything' does not exculpate because DeKalb County SO only dispatches for WPD. Provenance compounds it rather than rescuing it: 2024 is the agency's first year of any coverage at all, its declared NIBRS start of 2023-01-01 produced nothing whatsoever in 2023, and among pop 1,000-2,000 city agencies declaring 12 NIBRS months in 2024, first-year onboarders are ~7.6x enriched for near-empty submissions (22.8% at exactly 0 versus 3.7% of established reporters at <=2). At pop 1,417 - above the >1,000 line - an absent multi-year history plus a hollow first filing reads as an onboarding artefact, not safety, and every size-matched agency in its own county published 3-23. This is not the Georgia Military College shape: GMC carries FBIpop 0 and so has no resident population to generate index crime, whereas Waterman carries 1,417 residents and an operating patrol force. Lane agreement carries no weight here - CIUS is the Return-A master frozen at publication and SRS is at 0 months, so the three 2024 rows are one submission rendered three times.

rulings.detail: 30 must not stand as a measured full year comparable to 2020-2023. The stream split says which part is believable: rape 1, aggravated assault 14, burglary 3 and MVT 1 are credible as recorded across the 12 declared months; larceny at 11 against its own baseline of 489 is worth at most ~0-1 month of transmission. Mark the larceny stream unmeasured and forbid the 30-total from being used as a full-year level. Do NOT fill toward the 2021-2023 median of 517: the series is erratic (7, 97, 517, 495, 956), FBIpop is 0 in every year so the peer arm is blind and no per-capita rate can be formed, and the footprint is the Georgia statewide overlap layer - so leaving the larceny stream unmeasured costs almost nothing, while a 517-scale fill would be a large fabrication and would risk double-counting if those incidents moved to Columbus PD. Resolve by checking the 2024 Georgia state submission and whether the district still fields sworn officers.
rulings.rationale: This is the batch's cleanest composition-over-slope call, and the panel's own computed signal states it outright: retention across streams runs from 2.2% to 200% while the aggregate sits at 5.9%. Larceny went 489 to 11 (2.2% of its own baseline) in the very year aggravated assault went 7 to 14 (200%), moving aggravated assault from 1.4% to 47% of the year's total and larceny from 97% to 37%. A real change in the level of crime moves all seven streams together - and so, critically, does the competing benign hypothesis: an SRO transfer or staffing handoff to Columbus PD would cut the violent stream alongside the property stream, not double it. One stream doubling while the dominant stream vanishes is a change in which streams are present in the record, which is exactly what rules out the handoff reading the prior review could not dismiss. Month coverage cannot explain it either: NIB 12 months and SRS 11 months is near-full submission, unlike the true token cases in this batch where SRS collapses to 1-3 months. So the defect is stream transmission inside an administratively complete year - a token record published as complete.

rulings.detail: Do not carry 2 as a measured 12-month total. Believable content coverage is about one month - the SRS lane records 1 reported month for 2024 against the 12-month CIUS/NIBRS label - but do NOT apply the x12 uplift: 24 offences would be 1,375 per 100k, roughly twice the (1000,2500] peer median of 702.6, an indefensible repair off a 2-offence base. Flag the agency-year as token/partial, mark the property streams (burglary, larceny, MVT) unmeasured, and repair toward this agency's own pre-transition full-year level - 4 in 2018 and 6 in 2019, i.e. ~5 offences, ~290 per 100k, ~41% of the peer median. The all-zero 12-month NIBRS years 2021, 2022 and 2023 belong in the same treatment for the same reason; they are currently the reason the own-history arm reads a median of 0.
rulings.rationale: Composition flips completely, and that is the deciding fact. Every offence in this agency's own baseline record is property - larceny 4 and burglary 1 across the 2018-2019 CIUS full years, and 2020 SRS carried 6 larceny plus 4 MVT annualised - while 2024 carries only person offences (1 rape, 1 aggravated assault) with larceny, burglary and MVT all at 0. Larceny at 0% of a baseline of 4 for a town of 1,746 residents is not a reachable outcome; it is an untransmitted stream, and it is the same shape as the Muscogee County Schools case in this batch. That sits on top of the explicitly named structural pattern: an agency reporting 4-6 Part-I per year through 2019-2020 went to hard 12-month NIBRS zeros in 2021, 2022 and 2023 at pop 1,746, which is capacity-then-zero above the 1,000 threshold, and the break lines up exactly with its declared NIBRS start of 2021-01-01 - a transition failure, not a change in safety. The 2024 row shows the feed is alive (2 incidents got through, on a single SRS-recorded month) but still not carrying the streams that made up this agency's entire historic record, so the published 2 is a token record labelled as a complete year.
